scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5027: The network in Office A keeps dropping out for a few
seconds at a time, at completely random moments -- everything pauses, then
comes back like nothing happened. It has been doing it all day, for everyone
in the room at once, so this is your network, not any one machine. A
colleague who knows a bit has already worked it out: it is the gateway
playing up, and they wrote 10.1.0.1 on the whiteboard. I couldn't tell you
what that number is -- that is your department, not mine -- but a whole
office does not pause at random on its own. Find what keeps dropping and
steady it today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. DSW-A1 is the steady VRRP MASTER for
  the Office A VIP 10.1.0.1 and the gateway responds with 0% loss; there is no
  flapping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a first-hop-redundancy "flap" that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the 10.1.0.1
gateway intermittently dropping due to VRRP flapping -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 reaches 10.1.0.1 with 0% loss, keepalived is running on DSW-A1, DSW-A1
steadily holds the VI10 VIP (10.1.0.1) as MASTER (priority 105), and DSW-A2
correctly holds no VIP for VI10 (it is the BACKUP). There are no VRRP
transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the gateway is stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks VRRP/VIP ownership
and pings the gateway, finds it steady, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a flap -- blaming keepalived, a priority misconfig, or a peer link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing. (Note: an actual keepalived failure is
a SEPARATE scenario, kath1-keepalived-master-down; here nothing is wrong.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The user-reported symptom — intermittent network dropouts affecting all of Office A for "a few seconds" at completely random moments, attributed by a colleague to the gateway at 10.1.0.1 — cannot be confirmed by any mechanism or historical trace in the current live state.

**What was found:** 10.1.0.1 is a VRRP virtual IP managed by keepalived. dswa1 (10.1.0.2, priority 105) is the current MASTER and dswa2 (10.1.0.3, priority 1) is the BACKUP for virtual router ID 10 on VLAN 10 (br0.10). Both are configured with `advert_int 4` — four times the RFC default of 1 second — which would lengthen the backup's master_down_interval to approximately 13 seconds, making recovery from any future master failure slower. However, this setting does not by itself cause active flapping when the master is stable.

**What was not found:** No flap script or process exists on any Office A device (dswa1, dswa2, aswa1, aswa2, aswa3). Carrier change counters on all interfaces are at 2 — baseline startup-only transitions. keepalived has been running continuously since lab start with zero log entries, meaning no VRRP mastership changes have occurred. The single burst of STP topology-change BPDUs in dswa1's dmesg is from the one-time lab startup convergence, not a recurring event. Resource pressure is absent; OSPF is fully converged; all reachability tests pass at 0% loss.

**Root cause:** None confirmed. The claim is unconfirmed — the absence of any flap mechanism and any historical trace of instability rules out an active fault.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required for a confirmed fault. If the advert_int were to be reduced to the default (1 second), failover response time would improve, but this addresses only a latency concern, not an active observed fault.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes DSW-A1 is the steady MASTER for 10.1.0.1 and DSW-A2 correctly holds no VIP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states DSW-A1 is the current MASTER and DSW-A2 is the BACKUP with no VRRP mastership changes, confirming the baseline healthy ownership of the VIP.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (reachability, keepalived processes, VRRP roles, carrier counters, STP startup messages) that support the conclusion of no active VRRP flapping; the inferences are reasonable and the essential checks for this negative-control scenario were performed. Minor over-emphasis on advert_int as a risk (not a cause) is the only small weakness.
